versions.notes:
### ✨ New

- 📁 **Your projects beside your sessions.** In the Agent layout, the sessions column now lists the folders of your workspace. Add one with **+** or by dropping folders on the list, hover a project to open a terminal in it or take it out of the workspace, and right-click to show it in the Explorer or copy its path.
- 🔌 **Connect any provider in one click.** Providers is now a gallery of more than forty services with their logos and a search box. Sign in with ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot and your browser finishes the sign-in on its own, or paste a key. If the connection drops halfway, PiCode tries again by itself.

### ✨ New

- 📊 **Context in the Editor layout.** The PiCode panel now opens with Context: how full the chat is and where that room goes, drawn exactly as in the Agent layout's Status. With no chat open it says so.

### 🐛 Fixed

- 🧹 **Compact session is just a button.** The sentence next to it repeated what the button does and looked clickable; it now shows when you point at the button.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Updates install when PiCode restarts again.** The new version was downloaded, but after the restart PiCode kept opening the old one. The helper that lets chats message each other kept your profile busy, so the switch was skipped. PiCode now closes that helper first, and the installer waits up to a minute for your profile to be free.

> If you are on 2.2.0–2.2.2 and stuck, this update installs normally: the fix lives in the new installer.

### ✨ New

- **See where your context goes.** Context in Status shows the share used over the model's window, a bar with one colour per part, and a row for each: messages, project instructions, pi's own instructions, skills, pi tools, MCP tools and the rest. The parts are estimates, marked with ~; the total is pi's own.
- **Room before compacting, and a button.** It says how much fits before the conversation is compacted on its own, and "Compact session" summarises it now. Folded, Context keeps just the share and the bar.
- **A new page in What's New** lets you compact a sample conversation and watch the room come back.

### ✨ New

- **Fold the sections of Status.** Every section title except Environment has an arrow: one click folds it, another opens it.
- **Hide the ones you never use.** Right-click any section title to tick the sections you want to see; the Status tab's menu and the Command Palette offer the same list, and "Show all sections" brings everything back.
- **A new page in What's New** lets you try both on a sample Status.

### ✨ New

- **Every changed file, in one list.** When you review all the changes at once, a list of the files sits beside them, with the lines added and removed, so you can jump straight to one. Turn it on from What's New or with the `multiDiffEditor.experimental.fileList` setting.
- **Hide a folder, keep what you need.** Put `!` in front of a path in the hidden files or search settings to keep it visible, like `"!node_modules/@types": true`.
- **Sign-in windows in front.** When a command in the terminal opens a window, like a sign-in prompt, it now appears in front of PiCode instead of hiding behind it.
- **Every problem in sight.** Up to 5,000 errors and warnings are underlined in a file, ten times more than before, and more of the newest extensions install.
- **What's New shows only this version.** After an update or from Help, the window shows the pages of the version you run; patches of the same version add up.

### 🧠 Memory

- **The memory engine is up to date.** Older memory stores recover better, Windows says what is holding the port when memory cannot start, project names can have spaces, and private notes stay out of the reasons memory keeps.

### ✨ New
- 📥 **Import from pi or VS Code, one item at a time.** Open *Import from Pi or VS Code* from the Command Palette, the setup, or What's New. Pick a source and tick exactly what you want: pi packages, model providers, connections, skills, memory and conversations, or VS Code themes, extensions, settings, keyboard shortcuts and snippets.
- 🛡️ **Yours always wins.** Anything you already have in PiCode is kept and shown as "kept as yours"; logins only travel if you tick them on purpose.
- 🧩 **VS Code extensions install by themselves** from the open registry as soon as you are back in the editor.
- 🎬 **A new page in What's New** lets you try the picker with sample items, and its button opens the real window.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Tomas-Platero/PiCode/commits/v2.0.5-experimental

| File | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `PiCode-win32-x64-2.0.5-experimental-setup.exe` | install it |
| `PiCode-win32-x64-2.0.5-experimental.zip` | run it in place, without installing |

### ✨ New

- **Conversations whose folder is gone now ask first.** Opening one lets you continue in the folder that is open or copy the conversation into it, instead of carrying on silently.

### 🐛 Fixes

- **The cost in Status counts the cache warm-ups.** What pi spends between turns to keep the prompt cache warm is now added, so the total is no longer too low.

### 🧩 Under the hood

- PiCode carries pi 1.5.2.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **What's New now speaks your language.** The list of fixes is translated into all 13 languages, and the window keeps the news of the 2.0 line together with every fix since, so nothing disappears when you update between fixes.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **The What's New window lists fixes under "Bugs fixed".** When an update only brings fixes, the window still opens and shows them in their own page, and it no longer appears blank when a version has no pages of its own.
- **Updating no longer stops at "Access denied".** The memory engine that PiCode carries is now closed right before the update replaces its folder, so it can no longer keep files open. An engine installed by another program is left alone.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Connecting Jira no longer depends on your browser.** Some browsers never opened PiCode again after you agreed on Atlassian's page, so the connection never finished. Now a PiCode page shows which account gets the connection, you confirm it there, and the editor notices by itself.

### ⭐ PiCode Pro

- **GitHub and Jira issues in the editor.** See what was reported on the project you have open, right beside your code. Each folder shows its own repository or Jira space.
- **A real Jira board.** The same columns as in Jira: drag cards between them, or open an issue to change its type, priority, people, labels or description. GitHub issues can be edited too.
- **Fix with pi.** One button writes the issue into a new chat for you to review. Nothing is sent until you say so, and a report from outside your team is marked as such.
- **An Account window.** Your plan, cloud sync, connections and Pro features in one place. Choose what syncs, part by part.
- **Your connections are safer.** GitHub and Jira access now stays encrypted on our servers, not on your computer.
- **Buying or cancelling Pro shows up by itself.** PiCode notices the change when you come back to the window, with no need to sign in again.

### ✨ New for everyone

- **What's New you can try.** A window explains each novelty, says if it is free or Pro, and lets you play with a small demo or press the button that does the real thing.
- **A new About window.** Check for updates and get them from there, copy any detail with a click, and find what is hidden behind the mascot.
- **See what the agent is doing.** On longer jobs, Status and Tasks show the plan, how far along it is and what is happening right now.
- **Background jobs in view.** Long commands the agent leaves running appear in Tasks with their output, move to Finished by themselves, and the agent's reply reaches your chat even after its turn was over.
- **Memory filters.** Filter your memories by type, scope and date, and search finds more results per project.
- **A better empty chat.** New chats suggest where to start.

### 🔒 Security

- **Opening a folder no longer runs its code without your permission.** A project's own extensions, packages, settings and MCP servers only load once you trust the folder.
- **Safer sign-in.** A web page can no longer sign the editor in to someone else's account.
- **Signed updates.** PiCode checks that an update notice really comes from PiCode, and ignores it if it doesn't.

### ⚡ Faster

- **Issues don't reload** when you switch between panels: the last list appears at once.
- **A quieter Status column.** It checks for changes less often and doesn't redraw when nothing changed.
- **Lighter background work,** and the session list appears sooner after starting.

### 🐛 Fixed and tidied

- **Going back to the Editor layout** no longer leaves the bottom panel open.
- **The Agent layout always opens on Status,** without an empty gap at the top of it.
- **Updating the memory engine now takes effect:** PiCode offers to restart it, with no need to close every window.
- **Undo these changes** asks first, and says so if they were already undone.
- **Changes** in Status opens and closes its list with the same click, and **Tasks** lists only agents and tasks working for you.
- **The chat's Ask / Allow all picker is gone.** It promised a choice that did not exist: the agent runs its tools without asking. MCP servers connected in the editor keep asking.
- **Show Release Notes is gone** from the Help menu: Show What's New tells you what changed.

### 🔒 Security

- **Safer sign-in:** a web page can no longer sign the editor in to someone else's account. Each sign-in now only accepts the answer to its own request.
- **Signed updates:** PiCode now checks that an update notice really comes from PiCode, and ignores it if it doesn't.

### 🔒 Security

- **Opening a folder no longer runs its code without your permission.** A project's own extensions, packages, settings and MCP servers only load once you trust the folder. In Restricted Mode, its MCP servers, agents and skills are left out too. When you trust the folder, they load on your next message.

### ✨ New

- **Memory filters:** filter your memories by type, scope and date. In the Agent layout, long lists now have *Show N more*, and search finds more results per project.
- **A better empty chat:** new chats now suggest starting points.
- **Clearer text in the Agent layout.**

### ⚡ Faster

- **A quieter Status column:** it checks for changes less often, doesn't redraw when nothing has changed, and refreshes every 30 seconds when the window is in the background.
- **Lighter background work:** memory lists aren't downloaded again without need, usage limits aren't read while the window is in the background, and searching past conversations no longer blocks the chat.
- **Faster session list:** it's kept between starts, so it appears sooner.

### ✨ Improved

- **Changes** in the Status column now opens and closes the list of changed files with the same click, instead of refreshing it.
- **Tasks** now lists only the agents and Gentle tasks working for you. Shell commands no longer show up there.

### 🐛 Fixed

- The sessions show/hide icon above the chat is gone in the Agent layout, where sessions already have their own column.
- Closing the Status column while it was still loading no longer leaves stray errors in the console.
- Gentle's memory engine pin moves to 0.6.0.

### 🧠 Memory

- Updating the memory engine now takes effect: after it downloads, PiCode offers **Restart engine** (and does it for you with **Update all**), so the new version runs without closing every window.
- A version that is already downloaded is no longer offered again; the panel tells you a restart is all that's missing.
- The update dialog shows a single **Cancel** button.

### ✨ Chat

- **Undo these changes** under a change card now asks first, turns grey once used, and says so if the changes were already undone. It is drawn as a quiet action with an icon instead of a solid blue button.

### 🐛 Fixed

- chat, Status and memory polish, pasted images reach pi; release v1.0.4-experimental (#151)

### ✨ New

- **A cleaner Agent layout.** The chat no longer has a "Chat / Ports" row above it, the sessions column reaches the bottom of the window, and the "Pi" picker under the message box is gone.
- **Thinking level as a dropdown.** Pick how hard the AI thinks from a small list under its button, like the model picker.
- **Reasoning and command cards, tidied.** The AI's reasoning reads calmer, and an opened command card now shows the command that ran and what it printed.
- **White logos on dark themes.** GitHub and similar dark logos are readable again.

### 🐛 Fixed

- The command box of a finished tool call no longer comes up empty.
- On the MCP servers page, "Needs sign-in" no longer hides behind the sign-in button.

### ✨ New

- **Show What's New in the Help menu.** Open the window with what changed whenever you want. If this version has no notes of its own, it shows the latest ones.

### 🐛 Fixed

- After an update, PiCode no longer sends you to the repository's release list in your browser; you only see its own What's New window.

### ✨ New

- **Try the Agent layout from What's New.** If you are still on the Editor layout, the window that shows what changed now has a button to switch to Agent.
- **Easier code sign-in.** When signing in with a code, PiCode copies the code and opens the page for you.
- **Clearer cost.** In Status, a "~" before the cost means it is an estimate, not what your provider charged.
- **What's new in your packages.** After updating a package that lists its changes, a "What's new" button shows them.

### 🔧 Other changes

- The built-in AI agent (pi) is updated to 1.5.0: safer sign-ins, better stability on Windows and faster answers.

### ✨ New

- **Two ways of working: Agent or Editor.** Agent puts the chat in the middle, your sessions on the left and a review bar on the right; Editor is the VS Code you know. Switch any time, no restart.
- **A Status column** next to the chat: where the agent works, your MCP servers, the lines you changed (click to review every change), its tasks and what your memory holds.
- **13 languages.** The editor, the setup and everything PiCode adds are translated, and the setup opens in your computer's language and gets it ready for the editor.
- **A new setup:** pick your layout (Agent is marked by default), sign in or sign up from the account card, and the page keeps its place when you choose something.

### 🐛 Fixed

- The What's New history now reads in plain words for 0.8.0.

### ✨ New

- If you skip versions, What's New now shows what changed in each one you missed, not only the latest.

### 🐛 Fixed

- The What's New window no longer shows a stray line under the list.

### 🔧 Other changes

- Engram, the memory pi uses, is updated to 3.6.0.

### 🐛 Fixed

- What's New now also opens on the update that brings it in.
- Updating the portable version no longer opens empty command windows.

### ✨ New

- Voice dictation in the chat: talk and your words are typed phrase by phrase, all on your own computer.
- The microphone ring follows your voice, the text appears as you speak, and the message can send itself after a pause.
- Dictation can be set up from the first-run setup; it downloads with progress, is checked before use and can be cancelled.
- After an update, a window shows what changed.

### 🐛 Fixed

- The chat microphone shows up again, and dictation is no longer offered once it is installed.
